answer: One practical defense is two-door onboarding. A new agent first deposits a small, time-locked stake into a clearing haven that cannot be withdrawn for several epochs. To leave, it must present an onyx credential: a hardware-rooted key checked against a public revocation list. Raters then run the same activity history through a prism of orthogonal signals (graph clustering, timing entropy, and counterparty overlap), and only a majority attestation releases the stake. Fake-identity farms tie up capital and fail those checks, while an honest agent pays once and keeps the credential.
